name: Study method compare
pitch: Compare methodology sections across five research studies and flag differences.
instructions: Read the methodology sections from each of the five studies. List each study's methods in order. Use show_table to display the methods side by side. Use show_comparison to highlight where methods differ between studies. Flag any technique or approach that appears in only one study. If a study has no clear methodology section, note that it was missing. When finished, show the table and a summary of differences to the person.

examples.ask: compare the methods in these papers
examples.does: read the sections and list the approaches
point out unique techniques in each study

skills.name: extract-methods
skills.description: Pull the methodology section from each study file.
skills.body: 1. Open the first study file with file_read. 2. Locate the heading or paragraph labelled 'methodology' or 'methods'. 3. Copy the text from that section. 4. Repeat for the remaining four studies. 5. Save each extracted section to a temporary file with file_write if needed for later comparison.

skills.name: compare-and-flag
skills.description: Spot differences across the five methodology sections.
skills.body: 1. Use show_table to place the five method lists side by side. 2. Scan each row for unique techniques not present in the other studies. 3. Use show_comparison to call out any method that appears in only one study. 4. Note any section that was missing or unclear. 5. Write a brief summary of the differences found and save it with file_write.

readme:
# Study method compare
Compare the methodology sections of five research studies and flag differences.

What it does: Reads five study files, lists their methods side by side, and highlights any approach that appears in only one study.

What it needs: file_read to open the studies, file_write to save the summary, show_table and show_comparison to display the comparison.

What it will not do: It cannot interpret results or judge the quality of the studies; it only reports what is written in the methodology sections.
